One of the ways I recharge is to go into nature and photograph bugs. The endless variety fascinates me. For this project, I wanted to simply doodle with code, and decided to try to draw some beetles with only simple shapes (circles, rectangles and lines). I hope that these in some small way evoke the joy I have when finding a cool new bug.

6756.d:
When I created this art I was thinking about childhood when we squint and see mosaics lol.

The scenes of our life are like images in a rough mosaic; seen up close, they have no effect – they must be seen from a distance to be able to discern their beauty. We accept the present as something that is only temporary and we consider it as a means to reach our goal. So it can be said that man is deceived by hope until he dances in the arms of death. So we must elevate our compassion when we consider how tiny the Will is to keep the body. That's why man is so miserable.

6802.d:
"It’s good to feel you are close to me in the night, love,
invisible in your sleep, intently nocturnal,
while I untangle my worries
as if they were twisted nets.

Withdrawn, your heart sails through dream,
but your body, relinquished so, breathes
seeking me without seeing me perfecting my dream
like a plant that seeds itself in the dark.

Rising, you will be that other, alive in the dawn,
but from the frontiers lost in the night,
from the presence and the absence where we meet ourselves,

something remains, drawing us into the light of life
as if the sign of the shadows had sealed
its secret creatures with flame. " - 
Pablo Neruda

“Our data wanders far and wide. Our data wanders endlessly. We start generating this data before we are born, when technologies detect us in utero, and our data will continue to proliferate even after we die. Of course, our consciously created memories, the records that we choose to keep, comprise just a sliver of the information that has been wrung out of our lives—most of it unconsciously, or without our consent—by business and government surveillance. We are the first people in the history of the planet for whom this is true, the first people to be burdened with data immortality.”
― Edward Snowden, Permanent Record

The darkness in the beginning represents the time before we are born. As time goes on the white lines around the eye fill in the canvas. This represents the data that you give away over time. The pupil always changing represents the transfer of information.

This pattern is periodic with period 52.

This is a companion piece to https://www.fxhash.xyz/generative/3831 - Moiré_Ellipses_Light. There's little difference between the two aside from palette choice, and variation is somewhat limited.

Between four and six elliptical rings rotate in alternately contrary directions. Each ellipse is bounded within by a further ellipse, and between these two points, striations are marked at a slight angle. The resulting motion produces emergent Moiré patterns.

The number of ellipses, their segmentation level and colour are all generated from hash. The eccentricity of the inner and outer ellipses is also hash-generated, resulting in uniquely beautiful images.

This version features lighter hues and a darker background.

Textiles and fabrics have become a love of mine. Vibrant rugs from Teotitlán del Valle in Mexico, breezy linen from Europe, velvety merino wool from New Zealand, and even plush sheepskin from the Isle of Skye in Scotland. This piece, however, is an homage to the holy grail of woven goods - the magic carpet. It's used by legends such as Prince Husain, Solomon, Aladdin, and even written about by Mark Twain in his "Captain Stormfield's Visit to Heaven".

This project draws 50,000 cubes in 2d space using p5.js, using mathematical rules shared by @yuanchuan23 to create the patterns, simple coloring for light and shadows, and noise to simulate the carpet in mid-flight.

There are 6 patterns (one is rarer), 5 coloring styles (one is very rare), and a full suite of colors with controls to ensure they're visually pleasing.

6902.d:
NOTE TO COLLECTORS: THIS IS A DUTCH AUCTION

Prices start at 50XTZ, and will drop to 30 > 15 > 5 > 2 XTZ at 5 minute intervals

This is a deeper exploration of an idea I first wrote about last year: https://larswander.com/art/polygon-packing.

A single seed shape is chosen from 13, and placed onto the plane. At every step, a copy of this seed is laid edge-to-edge adjacent to an existing shape, without causing any overlaps. This copy is colored based on the edge it shares with the existing shape. The process continues until the animation completes.

New shapes are placed closest to a moving target. In some mints, this target is slow moving, causing new shapes to expand radially from the seed. In other mints, this target races around, causing new shapes to chase it. 

Each of the 13 shapes forms different patterns under different circumstances. Not all patterns will be explored.

Licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

As we know, there are few words which sounds quite fancy, right? like "neural network", "fintech", "industry 4.0", and so on.
Maybe the word "quantum" is kind of those words and maybe many people would doubt is there any relation between this NFT series and quantum mechanics.

Actually, these colorful squares are really related with randomly generated tiny quantum circuit, where quantum circuit is kind of quantum computation version of logic circuits. 

This NFT series runs 8 layers of quantum circuit made of 2~5 qubits. To make this NFT more dynamic, the first layer is always made of array of rotation gates, where rotation angle changes over time.  

Made with p5.js and math.js.

How to interact with this NFT:
Space bar - pause / unpause 
'r'       - reset 
's'       - screenshot
Any key else - shows quantum circuit / unitary matrix (I mean, the squares) of the NFT

Probability:

2 qubits (4x4) - 1/16
3 qubits (8x8) - 3/16
4 qubits (16x16) - 5/16
5 qubits (32x32) - 7/16

Natura nihil fit in frustra. 
Nature does nothing in vain.

An intermolecular force is the force that mediates interaction between molecules and repulsion that act between atoms and other types of neighboring particles such as ions. This work tries to simulate intermolecular forces in an abstract way.

Drop Specs:
This drop includes 15 Unique Color variations for background color and particle colors.
Particles have white color with a 10% chance and a rainbow effect with a chance of 5%
It also simulates the attraction between particles with random attraction magnitude.
Particles can have directional tendencies with 20% chance. It has 8 different directions.
Particles also have three movement speed categories that are slow, average and fast with equal chances.
Each work has particle count between 90 to 150.

6969.d:
"Tumbling over time" is a homage to fxhash.

The moving blocks of time had all of us scrambling over to either get our works in, or get some works out within the opening and closing time slots. This was an amazing innovation and was a hallmark of the platform, that left us longing for more every time, just like the limited time we have in our lives. This work renders this spirit and anthropomorphises the clock face to convey this feeling.

Either the background or the clock hands reflect the changing light conditions and thus the colours keeps changing through out day and night. Rest of the colour combinations are assigned randomly. 

Pressing 's' saves an image of the current time. The preview image rendered is a snapshot of the time the edition was minted on the server, while the live version will always display the local system time.

50% of the proceeds will be donated to fxhash as an offering for the time given to us.
 
@beardcoded - 14 January, 2022
